'''Daqing Wan''' (born 1964 in China) is a Chinese [[mathematician]], who after working in the [[United States]] for near 40 years, he moved to [[Chongqing University]] in 2025.<ref>https://www.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3345925/chinas-award-winning-mathematician-wan-daqing-leaves-california-chongqing</ref> He received his Ph.D. from the [[University of Washington]] in 1991, under the direction of [[Neal Koblitz]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Daqing Wan|id=28167}}.</ref> 

Between 1997 and 2025 he was on the faculty of mathematics at the [[University of California, Irvine]]. He also held visiting positions at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Pennsylvania State University]], the [[University of Rennes]], the [[Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute|Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]], and the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>[http://math.uci.edu/~dwan/vita.pdf Curriculum vitae] from Wan's web site.</ref>

His primary interests include [[number theory]] and arithmetic [[algebraic geometry]], particularly [[Riemann zeta function|zeta functions]] over [[finite field]]s. He is known for his proof of [[Bernard Dwork|Dwork]]'s conjecture <ref>{{citation |first=Bernard |last=Dwork |title=Normalized period matrices II |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=98 |issue=1 |year=1973|pages=1–57|doi=10.2307/1970905|jstor=1970905 }}.</ref> 
that the p-adic [[unit root zeta function]] attached to a family of varieties over a finite field of [[Characteristic (algebra)|characteristic p]] is [[p-adic]] [[meromorphic]].
<ref>{{citation |first=Daqing  |last=Wan |title=Dwork's conjecture on unit root zeta functions |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=150 |issue=3 |year=1999|pages=867–927 |arxiv=math/9911270 |doi=10.2307/121058|jstor=121058 |bibcode=1999math.....11270W |s2cid=18111544 }}.</ref> 
<ref>{{citation |first=Daqing  |last=Wan |title=Higher rank case of Dwork's conjecture|journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=13 |issue=4 |year=2000|pages=807–852|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-00-00339-8 |arxiv=math/0005309 |bibcode=2000math......5309W |s2cid=14898094 }}.</ref> 
<ref>{{citation |first=Daqing  |last=Wan |title=Rank one case of Dwork's conjecture|journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=13 |issue=4 |year=2000|pages=853–908|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-00-00340-4 |arxiv=math/0005308 |bibcode=2000math......5308W |s2cid=14824386 }}.</ref>

In 2001 he received the [[Morningside Medal|Morningside Silver Medal]] awarded to exceptional mathematicians of Chinese descent under the age of 45.<ref>[http://www.ims.cuhk.edu.hk/conference/iccm2004/Morningside.htm Morningside Award], retrieved 2010-01-27.</ref>

Wan, a renowned mathematician and former child prodigy, has left California to return to his hometown of Chongqing. Amid intense competition among Chinese universities, he has taken a new position in his home city.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-09 |title=China’s award-winning mathematician Wan Daqing leaves California for Chongqing |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3345925/chinas-award-winning-mathematician-wan-daqing-leaves-california-chongqing |access-date=2026-03-10 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}}</ref>
